steps.stem: Gilad wishes to verify that every worker in his factory who does not come to work by bus lives in the town itself. To which of the following questions must he receive the answer "no" in order to be certain of this?
choices: Is there a worker who comes to work by bus every day and lives outside the town?
Is there a worker who lives outside the town and does not come by bus?
Is there a worker who lives in the town itself and does not come to work by bus?
Are there workers from outside the town who arrive by bus?
explanation: The claim is: does not come by bus → lives in the town. Only a worker who does not come by bus and lives outside the town can break it, so Gilad needs a "no" to (2). (1) and (4) are about workers who come by bus, whom the claim does not cover; (3) asks about workers who simply fit the claim.

steps.stem: Three of the following claims have the same meaning. Which is the remaining claim?
choices: Every boat that has failed the safety test is not permitted to carry passengers
There is no boat that has failed the safety test and is permitted to carry passengers
If a boat is not permitted to carry passengers, it has failed the safety test
Only a boat that is not permitted to carry passengers can have failed the safety test
explanation: (1), (2) and (4) all say: failed the test → not permitted to carry passengers. (3) reverses the arrow (not permitted → failed).

steps.stem: A pair of claims is called "balanced" if each of the two claims can be inferred from the other. Which of the following pairs of claims is balanced?
choices: A. If the store is open, Orna is at work. B. If Orna is not at work, the store is not open.
A. There is someone who did not attend the meeting. B. There is no one who attended the meeting.
A. No painter in the group is without a studio. B. There are painters in the group who have a studio.
A. Every plant that is not watered wilts. B. Every plant that wilts is not watered.
explanation: B in (1) is A flipped and negated (the contrapositive), so each follows from the other. (4) reverses the arrow without negating; in (3) A does not guarantee that painters exist and B does not say all of them have a studio; (2) are different claims.

steps.stem: Given: the members of a certain quartet are left-handed violinists who live in Haifa. Which of the following questions can be answered on the basis of this information?
choices: Do left-handed violinists live in other cities as well?
Is this quartet the only group of left-handed violinists in Haifa?
Is every left-handed violinist who lives in Haifa a member of the quartet?
Is it true that none of the left-handed musicians who live in Haifa plays the violin?
explanation: The quartet's members exist and are left-handed musicians in Haifa who play the violin, so the answer to (4) is "no". (3) runs the arrow backwards; (1) and (2) ask about other cities and other groups, which the information does not mention.

steps.stem: The owner of a bakery found that in every month in which the bakery launched a new kind of bread, it spent more money on advertising, and as a result its profit in that month was lower than in the previous month. Which of the following cases, had it occurred, would certainly contradict this finding?
choices: A month in which the advertising expenses did not rise, but the profit was lower than in the previous month
A month in which no new kind of bread was launched and the profit was lower than in the previous month
A month in which no new bread was launched, but more money was spent on advertising
A month in which a new kind of bread was launched and the profit was higher than in the previous month
explanation: The finding says that a launch is followed by a lower profit; (4) has the launch without the lower profit. The finding says nothing about months without a launch, so (2) and (3) do not contradict it, and (1) does not say whether a new bread was launched.

steps.stem: Yoav: "Every book in this library that was printed before 1900 is kept in the basement." Dina: "Every book in this library that is not kept in the basement was printed after 1900." A book that was printed in 1950 and is kept in the basement -
choices: contradicts what Yoav said, but not what Dina said
does not contradict what either of them said
contradicts what both of them said
contradicts only what Dina said
explanation: Yoav: before 1900 → basement. Dina: not in the basement → after 1900, which is Yoav's claim flipped and negated. A book from 1950 kept in the basement meets neither condition (it was not printed before 1900 and it is in the basement), so it contradicts neither of them.

steps.stem:
A group of hikers went on a trip along a path that leads to a lookout point. It is known that:
- Every hiker who carried a map reached the lookout point.
- Every hiker who reached the lookout point returned before sunset.
If so, it is not possible that one of the hikers -
choices: did not carry a map and returned after sunset
carried a map, reached the lookout point and returned before sunset
carried a map and returned after sunset
did not reach the lookout point and returned before sunset
explanation: Map → lookout point → back before sunset, so a hiker with a map cannot return after sunset. The rules say nothing about hikers without a map or hikers who did not reach the lookout point, so (1) and (4) are possible; (2) is what the rules predict.

steps.stem:
Amnon visited the town library. It is known that:
- of the books in the library, Amnon leafed through all the books written in Spanish;
- all the books Amnon leafed through are hardcovers.
If so, it is not possible that the library has a book that -
choices: is in Spanish and is a paperback
is written in Italian and is a hardcover
is in Spanish and is a hardcover
is in Italian and is a paperback
explanation: In Spanish → Amnon leafed through it → hardcover, so a Spanish paperback is impossible. The rules say nothing about Italian books, and (3) is what the rules predict.

steps.stem: Which of the following pieces of information would make it possible to establish with certainty that every tile in the warehouse that is not glazed was made in Portugal?
choices: All the tiles not made in Portugal are glazed
All the tiles made in Portugal are glazed
Every glazed tile was made in Portugal
None of the tiles that were made in Portugal are glazed
explanation: "Not made in Portugal → glazed" is the flipped-and-negated form of "not glazed → made in Portugal". (3) reverses the arrow; (2) and (4) describe the Portuguese tiles, not where the unglazed tiles come from.

steps.title: Claims - the rules to know
steps.intro: Turn every claim into an arrow from the condition to the result.

tables.title: Reading a claim
head: The claim says
Arrow
What follows
rows: All A are B · If A then B
There is no A that is B
Only A is B · B only if A
A if and only if B

tables.title: Working with claims
head: Task
How
rows: join them through a shared term
look for the condition, or the negated result

tips: 'Only' at the start - reverse the arrow.
'Only' or 'every' mid-sentence: find what comes first - that's the condition.

steps.stem:
Below are three claims regarding the employees in a certain government ministry:
A. Tamar earns more than Yoav.
B. None of the employees in Yoav's department earns more than him.
C. Tamar does not work in Yoav's department.
Which of the following is true?
choices: If claims B and C are true, claim A is also necessarily true
Claim B can be inferred from claims A and C
If claims A and B are true, there is no possibility that claim C is not true
None of the three claims can be inferred from the other two, but also none of them contradicts the other two
explanation: A and B: Tamar earns more than Yoav, and no one in his department does, so she is not in his department - C cannot be false (3). B and C say nothing about Tamar's salary (1), A and C say nothing about Yoav's colleagues (2), and (4) is false because C follows from A and B.

steps.stem: A museum lends paintings to exhibitions abroad. Of the six works by a certain painter in its collection, three are oil paintings and three are watercolors. This year one of the watercolors was being restored, and four of the other five works were sent to an exhibition in Paris. Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: Both watercolors that were not being restored were sent to Paris
Exactly one watercolor was shown in Paris
Most of the works sent to Paris were oil paintings
At least two oil paintings were sent to Paris
explanation: Five works were available: three oils and two watercolors. Four were sent, so at most two watercolors and at least two oils (4). Two and two, or three oils and one watercolor, are both possible, which refutes (1), (2) and (3).

steps.stem: The advanced choir of a conservatory accepts only candidates who have passed an audition and, within a week of it, a written test in music theory. In addition, a candidate is accepted only if there is a free place in his voice range. Ronit passed both the audition and the written test, but was not accepted. Which of the following could explain this?
choices: Ronit's audition took place three days before her written test
There was no free place in the voice range in which Ronit sings
Ronit's written test was graded only after the results of the auditions had been published
Ronit had applied to the choir a year earlier and had been rejected
explanation: The three conditions are necessary; the only one that (2) says was not met is the free place. In (1) the test came within a week of the audition, so the conditions were met; (3) and (4) are irrelevant to the conditions.

steps.stem:
Every student in a certain boarding school participates in at least one of three activities: the orchestra, the choir and the drama club. It is known that among the students of the boarding school:
- no one who plays in the orchestra also sings in the choir.
- whoever does not participate in the drama club sings in the choir.
Which of the following is not possible?
choices: Hila plays in the orchestra and does not participate in any other activity
Hila participates in the drama club and also plays in the orchestra
Every student who sings in the choir also participates in the drama club
None of the students of the boarding school plays in the orchestra
explanation: Orchestra only means no drama club, so by the second rule Hila sings in the choir, which the first rule forbids for an orchestra player (1). (2) breaks no rule; (3) is possible if every student is in the drama club; (4) is possible.

steps.stem: Five members of a chess club played a tournament in which each member played one game against each of the others. None of the games ended in a draw. The club's chairman won all his games, and its youngest member lost all of his. Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: At least one of the other three players won exactly two games
The other three players each won the same number of games
The chairman won more games than any two of the other players together
No player won exactly three games
explanation: The three others each lost to the chairman and beat the youngest member, and played three games among themselves: either one win each (2, 2, 2 wins) or 2-1-0 (3, 2, 1 wins). Either way someone has exactly two wins (1). The 2-1-0 case refutes (2) and (4); in the 1-1-1 case two players together have 4 wins, refuting (3).

steps.stem: Zoologists studying a certain species of lizard hypothesized that the females lay their eggs only in sandy soil, where the eggs are protected from the heat. A survey of the area in which the species lives found that sandy soil occurs there only in a narrow strip along the coast, about two kilometers wide. A second survey, carried out a year later along the same strip, did not find a single egg of the species. Which of the following is true?
choices: The first survey weakens the hypothesis, and the second adds nothing to this
The two surveys together weaken the hypothesis, although neither weakens it on its own
The second survey weakens the hypothesis, but the first strengthens it
The surveys support the hypothesis, since they show that the lizards avoid the coast, where the soil does not suit them
explanation: If eggs are laid only in sandy soil, the first survey places them in the coastal strip and the second finds none there - only together do they weaken the hypothesis (2). Each survey alone is compatible with it.

steps.stem:
Claim A: Ofra invites to her home only people who do not invite her to theirs.
Claim B: Tzachi invites only Ofra, and Yoni invites everyone except Tzachi.
If both claims are true, Ofra -
choices: invites Tzachi and Yoni
invites only Yoni
does not invite either of them
invites Tzachi, but Yoni does not invite her
explanation: Tzachi invites Ofra, and Yoni, who invites everyone except Tzachi, invites Ofra too; since Ofra invites only those who do not invite her, she invites neither (3). (4) fails already on its second half.

steps.stem:
In a certain family there are four children. Their names, from the eldest to the youngest, are: Eliav, Orly, Tzuriel and Yifat. Each of them has brown eyes or blue eyes, and it is known that:
a. Eliav and Orly have eyes of different colors.
b. Every child in the family who has blue eyes has an older brother or sister with brown eyes.
Which of the following is not possible?
choices: Tzuriel and Yifat both have blue eyes, like their older sister
Yifat, the youngest, is the only one in the family whose eyes are brown, apart from the eldest
Three of the children have blue eyes
Orly has brown eyes
explanation: Eliav has no older sibling, so by b his eyes cannot be blue; they are brown, and by a Orly's are blue - (4) is impossible. (1): Eliav is the older brown-eyed sibling of all. (2): Eliav and Yifat brown, Orly and Tzuriel blue. (3): all except Eliav blue.

steps.stem:
Each of the four articles that were submitted to a certain journal was written in one language only - Hebrew or Arabic. It is known that of these articles:
A. only one was written in Arabic.
B. the number of articles that were rejected is greater than the number of articles in Hebrew that were accepted.
Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: The article in Arabic was rejected
At least three of the four articles were rejected
At least two of the articles in Hebrew were rejected
If the article in Arabic was accepted, then none of the articles in Hebrew was accepted
explanation: Let h be the number of accepted Hebrew articles and a = 1 if the Arabic one was accepted. Rejected = 4 - h - a > h gives h ≤ 1, so at least two of the three Hebrew articles were rejected (3). h = 1, a = 1 (two rejected) refutes (1), (2) and (4).

steps.stem:
Five runners participated in a race, and no two of them finished at the same moment.
Given:
- Moti finished after Nava and before Shula.
- Doron finished immediately after Shula.
- Hodaya did not finish last.
Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: Nava finished first in the race
Doron finished last
Hodaya finished in second place
Shula finished before Hodaya
explanation: Nava, Moti and Shula finish in that order and Doron right after Shula, so the last runner is Doron or Hodaya; Hodaya was not last (2). The possible orders are H-N-M-S-D, N-H-M-S-D and N-M-H-S-D, so (1) and (3) are not necessary and (4) never holds.

steps.stem:
Given:
- Some of the members of the photography club in a certain town are also members of the chess club.
- None of the members of the chess club lives outside the town.
Which of the following statements about the members of the photography club is necessarily true?
choices: Some of them live in the town
All of them live in the town
Most of them are also members of the chess club
If one of them lives in the town, he is also a member of the chess club
explanation: The members of both clubs are chess-club members, so they live in the town (1). Nothing is said about photography members who are not in the chess club, so (2), (3) and (4) do not follow.

steps.stem: An agronomist claims that in the orchard that he manages, only trees that bloomed early are pruned in the winter, and that an old tree never blooms early. Which of the following claims follows from the agronomist's words?
choices: If a tree in the orchard was pruned in the winter - it is not old
A young tree in the orchard that bloomed early is always pruned in the winter
If a tree in the orchard is not old, it bloomed early, but it was not necessarily pruned in the winter
Every tree that was not pruned in the winter is an old tree
explanation: Pruned → bloomed early → not old, so (1). (2) reverses the first rule (early blooming is necessary for pruning, not sufficient); (3) reverses the second rule; (4) reverses the whole chain.

steps.stem: According to the manufacturer of a certain incubator, whenever the temperature inside it rises above 38 degrees, a warning light comes on, and when it rises above 40 degrees, an alarm sounds as well. Which of the following, if it happened, would show that the manufacturer's claim is wrong?
choices: The warning light came on when the temperature inside the incubator was only 37 degrees
The alarm sounded while the warning light was off
The temperature reached 41 degrees and the warning light came on, but the alarm did not sound
The temperature stayed at 39 degrees for an hour, during which the light was on and the alarm sounded twice
explanation: The claim gives sufficient conditions only: above 38 → light, above 40 → alarm. Only (3), 41 degrees without an alarm, violates it. It does not say that the light or the alarm works only in those cases, so (1), (2) and (4) do not refute it.

steps.stem: According to the regulations of a certain poetry prize, the prize can be given only to a poet who has published at least two books of poetry, at least one of them within the five years before the award. The second condition does not apply to poets who have won the prize before, but the first does. Which of the following poets definitely cannot receive the prize this year?
choices: a poet who won the prize in the past and has published three books
a poet whose second book came out last year
a poet who has published two books, both of them seven years ago, and who won the prize in the past
a poet who never won the prize and whose last book, out of four, came out six years ago
explanation: (4) meets the first condition but has no book in the last five years and is not exempt. (1) and (3) are past winners with at least two books, so the second condition does not apply; (2) has two books, one of them last year.

steps.stem: Ilana told her friend that after a year of working with Yigal she had reached two conclusions about him: he will never refuse an assignment that involves travel, and it is possible that he will agree to an assignment that does not involve travel. Her friend told her that she is mistaken, and brought as proof an assignment that she had offered Yigal a month earlier. Which of the following could have been that assignment and Yigal's response to it?
choices: An assignment in the office, which Yigal agreed to only after he was promised a trip later on
An assignment that did not involve any travel, and Yigal refused it
A two-day assignment in Eilat, which Yigal refused
An assignment abroad, which Yigal accepted immediately, although he had said before that he was tired of traveling
explanation: Only a travel assignment that Yigal refused (3) refutes "he will never refuse". The second conclusion says only that he may agree, so one refusal of a no-travel assignment (2) does not refute it; (1) and (4) are consistent with both conclusions.

steps.stem: Eight delegates - two from each of four countries: Spain, Chile, Kenya and Japan - stayed in a hotel, two in each room, and no two delegates from the same country slept in the same room. In one of the rooms a delegate from Japan slept with a delegate from Spain. Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: In at least one of the rooms, a delegate from Kenya slept with a delegate from Chile
One of the delegates from Chile slept with a delegate from Japan
The second delegate from Japan did not sleep with the second delegate from Spain
Exactly two rooms were shared by delegates from Kenya and from Chile
explanation: The other three rooms hold one Japanese, one Spanish, two Chilean and two Kenyan delegates. At most two of the four Kenyans and Chileans can be paired with the Japanese and the Spanish delegate, so the other two share a room - and they cannot both be from the same country (1). The pairings J-S, K-C, K-C and K-J, K-C, C-S refute (2), (3) and (4).

steps.stem: In a certain poetry circle, members comment on one another's poems according to a fixed rule. Under this rule, Nurit may comment on Menachem's poems but not on Tzofit's, and Tzofit may comment on Nurit's poems but not on Menachem's. Which of the following could be the rule?
choices: Each member may comment on the poems of any member who joined the circle after him
A member may comment only on the poems of members whom he himself recommended for admission
Members of the same workshop group may comment on each other's poems
A member may comment on the poems of any member whose poems have not yet been published
explanation: (2): Nurit recommended Menachem, Tzofit recommended Nurit and not Menachem - no conflict. (1): Menachem joined after Nurit and Nurit after Tzofit, so Tzofit could comment on Menachem. (3) is symmetric, so Nurit could comment on Tzofit. (4): Nurit may comment on Menachem, so his poems are unpublished, and then Tzofit could comment on them too.

steps.stem: The heron greets only the frog. The otter trusts all the animals except those that the heron greets, and the eagle envies all the animals except those that the otter trusts. Therefore, the eagle envies -
choices: the heron and the otter
the frog only
no animal
all the animals that the heron does not greet
explanation: The otter trusts every animal except the frog, so the only animal the eagle envies is the frog (2). (1) and (4) name animals that the otter trusts, which the eagle therefore does not envy.

steps.stem: At a certain festival, every judge is a musician or a critic, but not both, and all the guests came from abroad. Adding which of the following statements makes it possible to conclude that none of the guests is a judge?
choices: Whoever came from abroad is a musician and also a critic
Whoever is not a judge came from abroad
Some of the guests are musicians who do not write criticism
Every critic from abroad also plays music, though not necessarily as a professional
explanation: With (1) every guest is both a musician and a critic, which no judge can be. (2) reverses the needed direction; (3) says nothing about the other guests; (4) leaves room for a guest who is a musician only and is a judge.

steps.stem:
In a certain office building there are four floors.
Given:
A. Only the third floor has offices with a balcony.
B. A coffee machine can be found only in an office that has a balcony.
C. In some of the corner offices there is a coffee machine.
Which of the following does not necessarily follow from this information?
choices: There is no coffee machine in any office on the fourth floor
At least one of the corner offices is on the third floor
Only corner offices have a balcony
Some of the offices that have a balcony are corner offices
explanation: The corner offices with a coffee machine have a balcony (B) and are on the third floor (A), which gives (2) and (4); an office on the fourth floor has no balcony and so no coffee machine (1). Nothing rules out non-corner offices with a balcony, so (3) does not follow.

steps.stem:
Below are four claims about the brothers Elad and Moshik:
A. Moshik has read the novel "The White City".
B. Elad has read every novel that Moshik has read.
C. Only one of the brothers has read "The White City".
D. Elad has read only one novel in his life.
The four claims together contain a contradiction. Which of them can be omitted without the contradiction disappearing?
choices: claim A
claim B
claim C
claim D
explanation: A and B mean that Elad has also read "The White City", which contradicts C. The contradiction stands without D; dropping A, B or C removes it (with D, Elad's one novel is "The White City").

steps.stem: A guide at a museum said: "Only the halls in the old wing have no air conditioning." Another guide said: "None of the halls in the old wing is air-conditioned." A visitor concluded that the hall in which the ancient maps are displayed, which is air-conditioned, is not in the old wing. On which of the guides' statements can the visitor's conclusion be based?
choices: On the first guide's statement only
Only on the two statements together
On the second guide's statement, even without the first
On neither statement, even when the two are taken together
explanation: The second statement says: old wing → not air-conditioned; hence air-conditioned → not in the old wing (3). The first says only that halls without air conditioning are in the old wing, which leaves room for air-conditioned halls there.

steps.stem:
The owner of a bookstore claimed:
- All the books with a hard cover in the store are in Hebrew.
- Every used book in the store is signed by its author.
A customer found in the store a book that proved both claims false. Which of the following cannot be true of this book?
choices: It has a soft cover
It is used and was printed abroad
It is not in Hebrew
Its author did not sign it
explanation: To refute the first claim the book must be a hardcover that is not in Hebrew; to refute the second it must be used and unsigned. So it is a hardcover and cannot have a soft cover (1); (2), (3) and (4) are all true of it.

steps.stem:
A certain residents' committee decided on the following procedure: a proposal is accepted if a majority of the committee members vote for it. At one of the meetings, the proposal to pave the old road was accepted. Afterwards, two claims were made about this vote:
A. Every committee member who voted for the proposal lives on the hill.
B. Not one of the committee members who live on the hill voted for the proposal.
Which of the following is true?
choices: Claim B follows from claim A
Claims A and B cannot both be true
If claim B is true, claim A is also necessarily true
Claim A is not consistent with the fact that the proposal was accepted
explanation: The proposal was accepted, so at least one member voted for it; by A he lives on the hill, and by B no one on the hill voted for it - a contradiction (2). B does not follow from A (1) nor A from B (3), and A alone is consistent with the vote if most members live on the hill (4).

steps.stem: In a certain museum, the old-map room is open to visitors only on Tuesdays and Thursdays. The drawers in which the maps are kept may be opened only when the curator is present, and the curator works at the museum only on Sundays, Mondays and Thursdays. Which of the following situations necessarily involves breaking one of the rules?
choices: On a Thursday, a group of visitors looked at maps that the curator had taken out of the drawers for them
On a Tuesday, visitors in the old-map room were shown a map that had been taken out of its drawer that morning
On a Monday, the curator opened the drawers to check the condition of the maps while the room was closed
On a Wednesday, the room was closed and the drawers stayed locked
explanation: On Tuesday the curator is not at the museum, so a drawer opened that morning was opened without him (2). On Thursday both the room and the curator are available (1); (3) and (4) break no rule.

steps.stem: An article on Hebrew translations states: "Of the novels of the nineteenth century that were translated into Hebrew, every one was either published in installments in a newspaper in its country of origin, or became a best seller there - but not both." Which of the following claims about four novels contradicts what is claimed in the article?
choices: A novel that came out in 1850, appeared in installments in a newspaper and became a best seller, and was never translated into Hebrew
A novel that came out in 1905 and was translated into Hebrew in 1930, appeared in installments and in the same year became a best seller in its country
A novel from 1872 that was translated into Hebrew, and appeared in installments in a newspaper; however, only a few copies of it were sold in its country
A novel from 1868, translated into Hebrew in 1911, that became a best seller in its country of origin after it appeared there in installments
explanation: The article covers nineteenth-century novels translated into Hebrew and allows exactly one of the two traits; (4) is such a novel with both. (1) was not translated, (2) is from the twentieth century, and (3) has only one trait.

steps.stem: A swimming club allows members under 16 to swim in the deep pool only if a lifeguard is with them or if they have passed the advanced swimming test. Which of the following situations breaks the club's rule?
choices: A 14-year-old who has not passed the advanced test swam in the deep pool while a lifeguard watched him
A 15-year-old who passed the advanced test last year swam alone in the deep pool
A 17-year-old who has never taken the advanced test swam alone in the deep pool
A 13-year-old who has not yet passed the advanced test swam in the deep pool with no lifeguard present
explanation: Under 16 in the deep pool requires a lifeguard or the advanced test; (4) has neither. (1) has a lifeguard, (2) has passed the test, and (3) is over 16.
